items.title: The locus where a section of an invertible module does not vanish is open and trivialises the module there
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement proves that for an invertible module on a ringed space with local local rings the nonvanishing locus of a section is open, that the section trivialises the module there, and that it admits an inverse section over the locus (author lemma at source lines 4576-4592, label lemma-s-open). The proof (source lines 4594-4618) uses the pairing with the inverse module and Nakayama's lemma to show that the section is a basis of the stalk at a point of the locus, then finds a neighbourhood on which the complementary basis element is represented by a section and on which the pairing is one, which shows that the neighbourhood lies in the locus and that the local inverse sections glue (proof lines 4595-4617). The Nakayama step and the gluing of the local inverse sections are the content. H2.
